title: Melyik jobb? Comparing Two Named Things

sections.title: The same -bb, a wider world
sections.content: You already use -bb + mint to compare weather, hotel rooms, and people. The exact same pattern compares anything you can name — two restaurants, two films, two cities — and jó still breaks the pattern the same irregular way: jó → jobb, not "jóbb". Ask about it with melyik ("which one"), a word you already know: Melyik jobb? ("Which one is better?")

sections.title: Comparing things
rows: Ez az étterem jobb, mint az.
This restaurant is better than that one.
A könyv érdekesebb, mint a film.
The book is more interesting than the film.

items.spanish: Melyik város nagyobb, Szeged vagy Debrecen?
items.english: Which city is bigger, Szeged or Debrecen?

items.spanish: Szerintem ez a film jobb, mint a másik.
items.english: In my opinion, this film is better than the other one.

sections.content: a másik ("the other one") is a handy stand-in for mint when you don't want to repeat the full noun — Ez jobb, mint a másik works for a restaurant, a film, or a room alike.
